---
title: Callout ids appear once in revealjs
format: revealjs
_quarto:
  tests:
    revealjs:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - - 'div.callout#titled'
          - 'section > div.callout#untitled'          # id-only callout: no wrapper
          - 'div.callout#tip-xref'
          - 'a.quarto-xref[href="#/tip-xref"]'
          - 'div.fragment > div.callout#with-fragment'
          - 'div[data-x="1"] > div.callout#with-attr'
          - 'div.fragment.test-no-id > div.callout'   # no-id wrapper unchanged
        - - '[id="titled"] [id="titled"]'
          - '[id="untitled"] [id="untitled"]'
          - '[id="tip-xref"] [id="tip-xref"]'
          - '[id="with-fragment"] [id="with-fragment"]'
          - '[id="with-attr"] [id="with-attr"]'
---

The revealjs callout renderer wraps the callout in a div carrying the
user's leftover attributes (classes such as `.fragment`, extra attributes).
The identifier must end up on exactly one element, the `.callout` div, and
an id-only callout needs no wrapper at all. A callout with a leftover
`data-*` attribute keeps it on the wrapper, and a callout with a fragment
class but no id keeps its wrapper unchanged.
